s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin fragility with seasonal variation and superficial erosions
salient_findings: Superficial skin erosions with linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
key_facts: 2-year-old girl presented with skin fragility
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Physical and mental developments were normal
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
Hair, nails, and mucous membranes were normal
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Skin biopsy showed complete separation of the stratum corneum
Genetic study revealed 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene

shortlist.label: Peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of skin fragility, superficial erosions, and seasonal variation matches this condition

shortlist.label: Acral peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction and seasonal variation are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Samira type peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic study revealing 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene supports this specific subtype of peeling skin syndrome

shortlist.label: Keratolysis exfoliativa
shortlist.why_kept: Mild xerosis and superficial skin erosions are consistent with this condition, although less specific than peeling skin syndrome

shortlist.label: Generalized peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and genetic findings could also be compatible with this more generalized form of peeling skin syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and erythematous residual macules, along with the genetic study revealing 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene, are consistent with peeling skin syndrome. The condition's improvement in winter and worsening in summer, as well as the lack of blistering, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acral peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: The lesions are not limited to acral areas, but are predominantly located at areas of friction

rejected.label: Samira type peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: There is no specific information in the vignette that suggests this rare subtype

rejected.label: Keratolysis exfoliativa
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a distinct pattern of peeling on the palms and soles, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Generalized peeling skin syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has widespread skin involvement, the specific genetic mutations and clinical features are more consistent with peeling skin syndrome
